summary: Idaho County lookout: 1934 pole tower, a 50-ft L-4 tower moved to Horseshoe Lake in 1962, gone there by 1983-85; sources conflict on the move.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab (1934); 50-foot treated timber tower with an L-4 cab (listed for 1953)
facts.status_note: Moved to Horseshoe Lake in 1962. That tower was gone from there by 1983 or 1985. Hartig's 1981 account says it was condemned and burned instead. No source describes the original site today.

corrections.why: Both lookout sites say the tower was moved to Horseshoe Lake in 1962, which fits 'moved to a new site' better than 'gone'. The loss in 1983-85 happened at Horseshoe Lake. Hartig's 1981 account says the tower was burned instead and is the only dissent.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, Kresek (via Forest Lookouts) and the register all tie the tower to a 1962 move to Horseshoe Lake. Hartig's 1981 account says it was condemned and burned near 1963. The story reports the move and notes Hartig.
Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1953. Hartig gives 1955. The story gives 1953 and notes 1955.
Firelookout.com says Clearwater National Forest. Idaho Fire Lookouts says St. Joe National Forest. The story reports both.

Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts date the pole tower to 1934. Hartig says the earlier structure it replaced went up before 1939. The story gives 1934 from the two lookout sites and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: The move to Horseshoe Lake is backed by four sites. Hartig's 1981 report is the only dissent. No source describes the original Indian Grave site today, so the 'today' paragraph says so. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the entry 'Drive-Up Moved' without saying which site it means. The Horseshoe Lake end of this history is also covered by us-id-horseshoe-lake, which has its own unresolved 1983 vs 1985 date. The brief's 'gone' status is proposed as 'relocated'.
